message.content: {"caption":"A side-by-side process comparison shows how using stored reasoning changes an online-shopping search from an incorrect answer based on recent orders to the correct first-purchase date.","description":"The diagram has two horizontal navigation sequences. The upper sequence, headed “Baseline (No memory),” shows small website screenshots labelled “Start on homepage,” “click (‘My Account’),” and “View ‘Recent Orders’ table.” A red outline highlights the Recent Orders view. To the right, the baseline answer says, “Your first purchase on this site was made on 3/11/23,” and is marked with a red cross. Beneath it, green text says to use memory item 5 and look for a link in “My Orders,” as mentioned in memory. The lower sequence, headed “Reasoning Bank,” shows screenshots labelled “Start on homepage,” “click (‘My Account’),” “View ‘My Orders’ table,” and “Next Page.” A green outline highlights the My Orders and Next Page views. The answer at right says, “Your first purchase on this site was made on March 2, 2022,” and is marked with a green check. The sequences progress from left to right; no arrows are shown. The tiny website contents are not legible.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
